review_candidates.title: Controller
review_candidates.description: Controller    About Mosaic Holdings  Mosaic Holdings is a permanent capital investment holding company; we acquire and partner with software businesses, holding them for the long term. We currently own portfolio companies operating across the US, Canada, the UK and Australia.  We recently closed a debt financing, which means we're entering a new stage: a first audit, lender reporting, and the need for accounting and finance operations that are reliable, organized and scalable across every company we own.  The role   The Controller owns accounting, payroll, taxes and compliance across all portfolio companies, reporting directly to the CFO. This is primarily an individual contributor role and not a management role: you'll work alongside our bookkeepers, an accountant, and a network of outside advisors (auditors, tax advisors) but will execute a lot of the work yourself.  You will help build and uplevel processes across the companies: close checklists, approval workflows, compliance calendars and the systems that help a growing group run smoothly. If you enjoy creating structure where there isn't any, and having a wide scope, this role is for you.  What you'll own   Month-end close   • Own the monthly close for each portfolio company  • Deliver consolidated financial statements monthly  • Give clear, constructive feedback to bookkeepers and raise the quality and speed of the close over time  • Improve and maintain close checklists, reconciliation standards and (eventually) a consistent chart of accounts across the group  Audit   • Lead preparation for our first financial statement audit (FY2027): build the audit calendar, prepare PBC schedules and serve as the primary contact for the audit firm  • Move companies from cash basis to accrual basis, where needed  • Write technical accounting memos on topics such as revenue recognition, acquisition accounting and capitalized software  Payroll, payables and approvals   • Take ownership of payroll for each portfolio company   • Review and approve vendor invoices and employee expense reports processed by the bookkeeper.  • Partner with the CFO on cash flow forecasts  Tax and compliance coordination   • Own the filing calendar for every company in every country, so nothing is missed  • Support ongoing lender reporting   • Work with our tax advisors in each jurisdiction: gather and hand over the documentation they need, answer their questions and make sure returns are filed on time  • Get ahead of issues we haven't yet addressed, starting with a US sales tax review, and stay proactive on new compliance requirements as we grow  Accounting operations and improvements   • Bring order to each company's accounting operations: documentation, implementing new software systems (for revenue recognition, for example), processes and controls  • Lead improvement projects across the portfolio and help integrate future acquisitions    What we're looking for   • 8+ years of accounting experience   • Hands-on experience preparing a company for audit and writing technical accounting memos under US GAAP  • A track record of building processes from scratch at small or fast-changing companies  • Comfortable managing outside advisors and keeping many deadlines moving at once  • A proactive, self-directed approach: you spot what needs doing before anyone asks, and you create structure rather than waiting for it  • Experience with areas not directly in accounting, such as payroll, insurance, reporting with Secretary of States, etc.    Nice to have   • Experience in public accounting (audit preferred)  • Experience in software or SaaS businesses  • Exposure to holding company, private equity or multi-entity environments, including consolidations and acquisition integration  • Experience with US sales tax nexus reviews and remediation  • Experience supporting lender reporting or debt covenants     Why join us   You'll be the first dedicated finance leader below the CFO, with real ownership and influence. Because we hold our companies permanently, the systems you build will last, and you'll see the impact of your work across the whole group. As Mosaic acquires more companies, this role is designed to grow.    Compensation and location   • Salary: USD $120,000 to $170,000 for US-based candidates  • Location: Remote, based in the US    How to apply   Send your resume and a short note to controllerapp@mosaicsoftwaregroup.com. In your note, tell me about an accounting process you built or improved: what you found, what you built, and what changed as a result.    The salary range for this role is posted above. Compensation at the time of offer is unique to each candidate and based on a variety of factors such as skill set, experience, qualifications, and work location. Salary is one part of Mosaic’s total compensation and benefits package. Other benefits for eligible employees may include paid time off and health benefits offerings. Please note, the base salary range listed below and the benefits in this paragraph are only applicable to U.S.-based candidates.     Mosaic does not accept unsolicited resumes or candidate submissions from external agencies or recruiters. All candidates must apply as noted above. Any resumes submitted by agencies without a prior signed agreement will be considered unsolicited and Mosaic will not be obligated to pay any fees.

review_candidates.description: Compliance Manager –Fintech International Operations Company:  Omits Financial & Technology Inc. (Omits) Location:  Nigeria (Remote) Employment Type:  Full-Time Department:  Risk & Compliance Reporting To:  Chief Executive Officer / Head of Operations Industry:  Fintech | Cross-Border Payments | Financial Services Salary: N1,200,000 -N1,500,000 About Omits Omits is a growing international financial technology company building a modern platform for cross-border payments, multi-currency financial services, and global money movement. Headquartered in Canada, with operations and expansion initiatives across the United Kingdom, United States, Nigeria, and other international markets, Omits is committed to making global financial transactions simpler, faster, more accessible, and more transparent. As we expand our international footprint, we are strengthening our compliance leadership to support our regulatory obligations, financial institution partnerships, and long-term growth. Position Overview We are seeking an experienced, highly professional, and commercially minded  Compliance Manager – International Operations  to lead and coordinate compliance activities across our international operations. The ideal candidate will combine strong technical expertise in financial services regulation, AML/CTF, sanctions compliance, transaction monitoring, and regulatory risk management with exceptional communication, leadership, and stakeholder engagement skills. This is a hands-on management role requiring someone capable of both developing compliance frameworks and overseeing their practical implementation. The successful candidate must be comfortable engaging with senior executives, banking partners, regulators, external auditors, and internal operational teams across multiple jurisdictions. Key Responsibilities 1. International Regulatory Compliance Oversee and coordinate compliance requirements across Omits' operations in Canada, Nigeria, the United Kingdom, the United States, and other expansion markets. Maintain working knowledge of applicable regulatory frameworks, including FINTRAC, the Bank of Canada's Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA), FCA, FinCEN, and relevant Nigerian regulatory requirements. Monitor regulatory developments and assess their impact on Omits' products, operations, and international expansion. Maintain compliance obligations registers, regulatory calendars, policies, and reporting schedules. Support regulatory applications, registrations, examinations, and ongoing compliance obligations. Work with designated compliance officers, MLROs, and external advisers to ensure jurisdiction-specific requirements are met. 2. AML/CTF and Financial Crime Compliance Oversee the implementation and continuous improvement of the company's AML/CTF and financial crime compliance programs. Supervise customer due diligence (CDD), enhanced due diligence (EDD), KYC/KYB, sanctions screening, PEP screening, and adverse media processes. Oversee transaction monitoring, suspicious activity investigations, and escalation procedures. Ensure appropriate handling of high-risk customers, unusual transactions, and potential financial crime exposure. Coordinate suspicious transaction reporting and other regulatory reporting requirements with designated responsible officers. Maintain appropriate controls for cross-border payments and high-risk corridors. 3. Compliance Team Leadership Manage and supervise Compliance Officers and Compliance Analysts across multiple locations. Establish clear responsibilities, performance expectations, and operational procedures. Review complex compliance cases and provide guidance on risk-based decisions. Ensure timely completion of onboarding reviews, transaction investigations, and compliance escalations. Develop training programs and support the professional development of compliance personnel. Promote accountability, consistency, and high standards of professional conduct. 4. Banking and Regulatory Partner Management Serve as a senior compliance contact for banking partners, payment service providers, and other financial institutions. Coordinate responses to partner due diligence requests, compliance questionnaires, audits, and ongoing monitoring requirements. Support onboarding and maintenance of international banking and payment partnerships. Prepare professional compliance presentations, reports, and supporting documentation. Participate in meetings with international stakeholders and represent Omits with professionalism and confidence. 5. Risk Management and Internal Controls Conduct and maintain business-wide and product-specific compliance risk assessments. Identify compliance gaps and recommend practical, risk-based remediation measures. Oversee compliance monitoring, internal reviews, control testing, and remediation tracking. Collaborate with Product, Engineering, Operations, and Finance to embed compliance requirements into business processes. Support the implementation and improvement of automated compliance systems, including transaction monitoring and fraud prevention tools. Ensure proper recordkeeping, documentation, and audit readiness. 6. Governance and Management Reporting Prepare periodic compliance reports for senior management. Track compliance KPIs, incidents, investigations, regulatory changes, and outstanding remediation actions. Escalate material compliance risks promptly and appropriately. Contribute to compliance policies, governance frameworks, and operational decision-making. Support strategic initiatives, new market entry, and product launches from a regulatory perspective. Required Qualifications and Experience Bachelor's degree in Law, Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Economics, or a related discipline. Minimum 7 years of relevant experience  in compliance, financial crime, regulatory affairs, or risk management. At least 3 years of experience in a supervisory, management, or senior compliance role. Experience within fintech, payment services, remittances, digital banking, or other regulated financial institutions. Strong practical knowledge of AML/CTF, KYC/KYB, sanctions compliance, transaction monitoring, and regulatory reporting. Demonstrated experience developing, implementing, or managing compliance frameworks. Experience working with international regulatory standards or cross-border financial services. Strong written and spoken English, with the ability to communicate effectively with international stakeholders. Proven ability to manage teams, prioritize competing demands, and exercise independent professional judgment. Preferred Qualifications Professional certifications such as CAMS, ICA, CFE, or equivalent. Direct experience with Canadian FINTRAC requirements, UK FCA regulations, US FinCEN requirements, or Nigerian financial services regulations. Experience supporting regulatory examinations, banking partnerships, or payment institution licensing. Familiarity with compliance technology, automated transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, and identity verification platforms. Experience managing distributed or remote compliance teams. Prior experience with an international fintech or multinational financial institution. Key Competencies Executive-Level Communication:  Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with the confidence and professionalism to engage senior stakeholders. Technical Competence:  Strong understanding of regulatory compliance and the ability to translate requirements into practical controls. Leadership:  Ability to supervise, coach, and hold compliance personnel accountable. Sound Judgment:  Ability to make balanced, risk-based decisions while maintaining regulatory integrity. Attention to Detail:  High standards of accuracy, documentation, and follow-through. Commercial Awareness:  Understanding of how compliance supports responsible business growth without compromising regulatory obligations. Ownership and Initiative:  Proactive, independent, and comfortable working in a fast-growing environment. Working Arrangements Fully remote position based in Nigeria. Full-time employment. Regular collaboration with teams and stakeholders in Canada, the United Kingdom, the United States, and other international markets. Flexibility to attend occasional meetings across international time zones. Performance-driven environment with significant opportunities for professional growth. What We Offer Opportunity to play a key leadership role in a growing international fintech company. Exposure to multiple international regulatory environments. Direct engagement with senior management and international financial partners. Opportunity to shape and strengthen the company's global compliance infrastructure. Competitive compensation based on qualifications and experience. Long-term career growth as Omits expands internationally. How to Apply Interested candidates should submit their CV and a brief cover letter outlining their relevant compliance management experience, international regulatory exposure, and leadership background. Omits – Your money. More Possibilities.
